title: Tail bound for a biased Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $p\in[0,1]$, and let $S\subseteq[n]$. Choose a random function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ by assigning independent values, each equal to $1$ with probability $p$ and $0$ otherwise. The probability that the absolute difference between its $S$-th Fourier coefficient (after viewing its values as real numbers) and $p$ when $S=\varnothing$, or $0$ otherwise, is at least $2\sqrt n\,2^{-n/2}$ is at most $2\exp(-2n)$.
